jobs.title: Spatial Analyst, Clerk Grade 5/6, Wollongong or Rhodes
jobs.location: Concord West, New South Wales, Australia
jobs.description:
Spatial Analyst, Clerk Grade 5/6, Wollongong

Showcase your GIS capabilities and provide data visualisation tools, maps and dashboards that will support NSWSES staff and volunteers with planning and operational response
Work in a volunteer-based agency supporting communities of NSW
Fulltime, ongoing role
Location: Wollongong at NSW SES State Headquarters, with consideration for Rhodes at Metro Headquarters for an exceptional applicant. Hybrid working arrangements available.

About the opportunity

Are you passionate about spatial data, analytics, and technology? This is an exciting opportunity to leverage your expertise in GIS, spatial analysis, and data visualisation to deliver impactful Geospatial Intelligence products and services. Working within the Emergency Management Directorate, you will help drive innovation, support critical operations, and transform complex spatial information into actionable intelligence for NSW SES.
Tasks include:
Design and deliver innovative GIS solutions, undertake complex spatial analysis, and develop high-quality geospatial products including maps, dashboards, and field collection tools.
Support effective administration of the NSW Flood Data Portal and flood data management services
Support AIIMS Mapping Officer role in Operational response

About the NSW SES

Our Mission: NSW SES saving lives and creating safer communities.
Our Vision: A trusted volunteer-based emergency service, working together to deliver excellence in community preparedness and emergency response.

The NSW SES serves the community as the lead agency for Floods, Storms and Tsunamis. We are recognised as the most versatile and widely used emergency service organisation in NSW. Our volunteers are highly skilled, experienced, and well- trained in the wide variety of roles they perform.

With over 10,000 volunteers we are committed to protecting and supporting the diverse communities of NSW. Learn more here.

About you

To be successful in this role you will:
hold relevant tertiary qualifications/ and or experience in GIS/spatial information, in particular ArcGIS Enterprise, ArcGIS Pro and VertiGIS Studio;
have prior experience in the administration and maintenance of GIS including ArcGIS portal administration, effective database management and advanced spatial analysis such as use of SQL server, FME or python;
Understand the geospatial application development lifecycle and apply GIS research, best practice, standards, and architecture to support and align business and operational processes
Possess excellent presentation and written communication skills to lead the delivery of GIS training, coordinate volunteer mapping initiatives for operational response, and fulfil Mapping Officer role as required.

What we can offer you

You will enjoy a 35-hour work week, with the potential for flexible work arrangements.
You can enjoy a hybrid work environment, time in the office and time working from home.
Attractive salary range of $102,936 to $113,579 plus 12% superannuation and leave loading
Our work is meaningful and rewarding. The SES’s mission is saving lives and creating safer communities and you can be an important part of our work.
We have attractive leave entitlements including parental, sick, flex and recreation leave.
We care about our people. We have Mental Health & Wellbeing programs and services to support our people and operational and leadership training and development opportunities to develop our people. Some of these include:
Fitness Passport
LinkedIn Learning
Member Assist Program for free confidential counselling support
Immunisation program.

You Belong Here

We care about people as individuals and are committed to diversity, inclusion, and new ways of working. We encourage applications from people of any age, gender, ethnicity, cultural background, faith, disability, sexual orientation or gender identity.
We want our people to reflect the diverse community we serve and are committed to creating an inclusive and flexible workplace. We want to know what this looks like for you so we can support your success at work.
If you require reasonable adjustments, we are committed to supporting you throughout the recruitment processes and in the workplace, if you feel you may require an adjustment during the recruitment process, please contact recruitment@ses.nsw.gov.au for confidential advice on options.

How to apply

Your application should include as separate attachments:
A cover letter (maximum of one page) briefly responding to the essential requirements
and your interest in the role;
Responses to each of the targeted questions
(maximum of one page per answer); and
An up-to-date resume
of no more than four pages detailing your skills and experience relevant to the role

Targeted Questions

Outline your skills and experience in managing complex and large spatial datasets (including vector and imagery), and utilising that data to create products across a range of geospatial delivery platforms
Provide an example of how you have been able to utilise GIS to provide innovative geo-solutions for customers. Please outline your development process, how you managed stakeholders and resources, and the outcome achieved.

jobs.description:
Job Overview

Are you passionate about the environment, love working outdoors, and have a background in air, noise and water environmental technician work? We are seeking a talented and self-motivated Field Environmental Technician to join our team. This project contract role offers a unique opportunity to work in the field and contribute to the preservation and sustainability of our natural resources.
Field Environmental Technician Responsibilities & Duties
Core role: Conduct field work to collect environmental data, including: Establishment, operation, management of various air quality monitoring networks including: fine particulates, dust fallout; trace gas pollutants; meteorology etc. Undertaking day and night-time noise surveys with sound level meters. Environmental monitoring services may be expanded to include surface/ground water and soil sampling etc. Gathering of accurate environmental data and physical samples from field sites to support compliance monitoring and research. Use scientific equipment to record environmental parameters including but not limited to: Various hand held environmental monitors, sound level monitors, passive badge samplers, SANS 1137 dust fallout monitors, GPS, calibration equipment, fine particulate monitors, etc. Assist in the planning and execution of environmental monitoring projects.
Work Environment: Mix of outdoor fieldwork in varying weather conditions and at various times of the day (i.e. included day and night-time surveys) and indoor office or lab work for reporting. This position requires extensive travel away from the office (i.e. >50% of the time) as is primarily a fieldwork position and thus the candidate must be willing and able to travel based on ATB’s needs.
Sample collection and equipment care: Set up, operate, and calibrate field testing instruments and monitoring devices in and laboratory and field environment. Gathering of air, noise, dust samples using specialized scientific equipment. Sample collections may be expended into soil, surface water, groundwater fields.
Data Tracking: Maintain up-to-date records of field activities, results, accurate chain-of-custody documentation, field logs, and photo logs. Communicate findings to team members, clients, and stakeholders.
Health and safety : Comply with all health and safety regulations and procedures typical of mining and industrial manufacturing market sector clients. Follow strict health protocols and wear required personal protective equipment (PPE). Examine project areas for health and safety risks to allow for safe working in the field. The employee will often be required to work alone in the field and during the day and night and thus a good grip on safety procedures and following safety protocols is critical.

Field Environmental Technician Qualifications & Skills
1-2+ years of experience as an air, dust, noise environmental field technician or in a related role. Previous fieldwork or internship experience in environmental monitoring or related areas
Basic knowledge and understanding of environmental regulations and compliance practices
Proficiency in using environmental testing and sampling equipment for air, noise, dust (as a minimum). Additional experience in water and soil equipment advantageous
Strong analytical and infield problem-solving skills
Excellent written and verbal communication abilities
Ability to work independently and in a team environment
Experience with data analysis software and reporting tools
Ability to use testing tools, record precise data, and basic computer proficiency including Microsoft word, Excel, Google Earth, Internet and Email 
Excellent organizational and record-keeping abilities
Valid driver's license for extensive travel to different job sites (non-negotiable)
Reliable vehicle allowing travel to and from the office
Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Biology, Chemistry, or related field and/or certifications related to environmental technology or science (advantageous)
Our clients undertake regular drug and alcohol screening and thus the contract employee must be of sober habits and not use any recreational drugs whatsoever  

Renumeration
This is a project-based 12-contract post (Renewable based on ATB’s various project needs).
Market related renumeration and based on experience
How to apply to the post:
If you are considering joining our team and would like to apply for the contract position, we will be running a candidate pre-screening process followed by formal interviews of the shortlisted candidates.
To apply please submit the following to admin@atbenviro.co.za:
·       Detailed CV listing qualifications and experience
·       Certified copies of qualifications from universities, Technicon’s etc
·       Certified copy of ID and Drivers licence
·       Three contactable references of people/clients you have undertaken environmental fieldwork for
·       Cost to company salary expectation    
If you have not heard back from ATB within 2 weeks of the closure date, consider your application unsuccessful:
Closure date: 2 October 2026 @10am

jobs.description:
Find Your Future With Us at USDA – Animal Plant Health Inspection Service

Job Summary

This position is with the National Wildlife Research Center (NWRC), Management of Ungulate Damage and Disease (MUDD) Project located in Fort Collins, CO. The work is primarily concerned with wildlife damage management (WDM) research relating to the assessment, reduction, and/or elimination of problems associated with wild and/or feral swine in urban, suburban, and rural environments.

Qualifications

Applicants must meet all qualifications and eligibility requirements by the closing date of the announcement, including specialized experience and/or education, as defined below. BASIC REQUIREMENT: Degree: biological science that included: At least 9 semester hours in such wildlife subjects as mammalogy, ornithology, animal ecology, wildlife management, or research courses in the field of wildlife biology; and At least 12 semester hours in zoology in such subjects as general zoology, invertebrate zoology, vertebrate zoology, comparative anatomy, physiology, genetics, ecology, cellular biology, parasitology, entomology, or research courses in such subjects (Excess courses in wildlife biology may be used to meet the zoology requirements where appropriate.); and At least 9 semester hours in botany or the related plant sciences. OR Combination of education and experience: equivalent to a major in biological science (i.e., at least 30 semester hours), with at least 9 semester hours in wildlife subjects, 12 semester hours in zoology, and 9 semester hours in botany or related plant science, as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education. In addition to the basic requirement applicants must also possess: FOR THE GS-09 LEVEL: Applicants must have one year of specialized experience (equivalent to the GS-9 level) that may have been obtained in the private or public (local, county, state, Federal) sectors which demonstrates: Working knowledge and experience related to a variety of technical procedures used in wildlife biology including animal capture, restraint, marking, and transport; collection and preservation of biological data and samples; chemical immobilization; and animal euthanasia and necropsy. Ability to gather, organize, and analyze data using techniques and technologies such as telemetry, GPS, GIS, web-based systems for data entry, app development for data entry, and administrative processes, wildlife population census and surveys, and wildlife monitoring and surveillance. Good Laboratory Practices training and experience for evaluating new pesticides for feral ungulates. Experience leading research teams in remote, sometimes dangerous, field settings for data collection activities. Proficiency in evaluating the risks of foreign animal diseases from feral ungulates to domestic livestock. Background in handling feral swine and deer, attaching GPS collars and ear tags, and monitoring their movements. OR 2 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree or master's or equivalent graduate degree in one of the following degree fields: Wildlife Biology, Wildlife Ecology, or Wildlife Management or closely related field. Equivalent combinations of education and experience are qualifying for this grade level. TRANSCRIPTS are required if: This position requires specific coursework or a degree in a specific field to be basically qualified. You are qualifying for the position based on education. You are qualifying for this position based on a combination of experience and education. This education must have been successfully completed and obtained from an accredited school, college, or university. COMBINATION OF EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE AT THE GS-09 GRADE LEVEL: Applicants may have combinations of successfully completed education and specialized experience to meet total qualification requirements. The total percentages must equal at least 100 percent to qualify for that grade level. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Progettazione, analisi e sviluppo di sistemi Laser/LiDAR

.

per applicazioni spaziali.

Capacità di lavorare su architetture di sistema e di gestire requisiti tecnici.
